answer_items.answer: Micron Technology Inc. states that Singapore's global minimum tax, specifically the 15% minimum tax Pillar Two Model Rules, affects their taxes by largely offsetting the benefit from their Singapore tax incentive arrangements. Micron Technology Inc. also mentions that Singapore enacted legislation to implement Pillar Two, which will apply to them starting in 2026, and they continue to monitor for additional guidance and legislative changes related to Pillar Two in the jurisdictions where they operate. Micron Technology Inc. indicates that the aggregate impact of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) remains uncertain, and they will continue to monitor future developments, including regulatory guidance and interpretations, which could have a material impact on their income tax provision. Applied Materials Inc. states that Singapore's global minimum tax affects their taxes by materially increasing their foreign taxes beginning in the first quarter of fiscal 2026, primarily due to the implementation of the global minimum tax regime in Singapore. Applied Materials Inc. also mentions that the global minimum tax regime in Singapore has led to a remeasurement of deferred tax assets resulting in a lower effective tax rate for the first nine months of fiscal 2026.
